45wwzh:429: Wiz's AI Threat Readiness framework is built on two dimensions: Speed of Action and Breadth of Visibility. These two axes form the foundational coordinates for all security operations work. The core question on the speed axis: can the organization complete the full identify-validate-remediate loop before attackers do? As AI accelerates vulnerability discovery, every stage of this loop needs to be re-optimized. Traditional discrete processes (discovery is one team, validation another, remediation a third) are now a bottleneck, because the delay between each step can be exploited by attackers. The visibility axis focuses on whether the organization truly knows what it has exposed. Wiz's data reveals a key insight: what is dangerous is often not known high-severity vulnerabilities, but forgotten exposure surfaces. 30% of cloud environments have high-impact machines exposed—not because these machines have known CVEs, but because they are exposed to the internet and their software versions may contain unknown vulnerabilities. More notably, 19% of exposed software resides on systems with IAM privileges, meaning attackers can use these systems as a springboard to access sensitive internal assets.
8bnylf:146: — When exposure cannot be fully eliminated (which is the norm in real environments), the key becomes whether remediation can be completed faster than attackers. This requires clear ownership, prioritization, and execution paths. The article specifically emphasizes the importance of distinguishing three types of vulnerabilities: third-party software vulnerabilities (CVEs), instances of those vulnerabilities in the environment, and vulnerabilities in first-party code. Each type requires different detection, prioritization, and remediation strategies.

The metric system should cover the full-cycle time from exposure discovery to remediation completion (MTTR), as well as coverage rates at each layer.
